comparisons.peer_summary: The Company offers a 401(k) plan in the US with a matching contribution of 75% of employee contributions up to 6% of eligible compensation, resulting in Company contributions of approximately $78 million, $70 million, and $47 million in 2024, 2023, and 2022 respectively.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and AMD disclose expenses related to defined contribution plans (401(k)/tax-qualified) for eligible employees. NVDA reports total contribution expenses of $255 million in 2024 for plans in the U.S. and certain other countries, with a general statement of providing tax-qualified plans. AMD specifically details its US 401(k) plan structure, noting a 75% match up to 6% of compensation, and reports company contributions of approximately $78 million in 2024. While both address employee retirement savings contributions, NVDA's disclosure aggregates expenses across multiple jurisdictions without specifying the matching formula in the cited text, whereas AMD explicitly defines the US plan's matching structure but only provides the contribution amount for the US plan.

sentences.text: We provide tax-qualified defined contribution plans to eligible employees in the U.S. and certain other countries.
Our contribution expense for fiscal years 2024, 2023, and 2022 was $255 million, $227 million, and $168 million, respectively.
The Company provides retirement benefit plans in the United States and certain foreign countries.
The Company matches 75% of employees' contributions up to 6% of their eligible compensation.
The Company's contributions to the 401(k) plan for 2024, 2023 and 2022 were approximately $78 million, $70 million and $47 million, respectively.

comparisons.peer_summary: Eligible employees outside the U.S. receive retirement benefits under various defined contribution plans.
comparisons.comparison: NVDA and Broadcom (AVGO) both disclose the provision of defined contribution retirement plans to eligible employees. NVDA states it provides tax-qualified defined contribution plans to eligible employees in the U.S. and certain other countries, while AVGO states that eligible employees outside the U.S. receive retirement benefits under various defined contribution retirement plans. Both disclosures confirm the existence of these plans as a benefit for their workforce, though the cited AVGO sentence specifically highlights international participation while the NVDA text covers both US and international scope.

sentences.text: We provide tax-qualified defined contribution plans to eligible employees in the U.S. and certain other countries.
In addition, other eligible employees outside of the U.S. receive retirement benefits under various defined contribution retirement plans.

comparisons.peer_topic: Retirement Plan Expenses and Matching Contribution Changes
comparisons.peer_summary: Matching contribution expenses were $541 million in 2024, $272 million in 2023, and $489 million in 2022. The matching contribution rate in the US qualified plan was increased in 2024 compared to prior years but was reduced in 2023 compared to 2022.
comparisons.comparison: Both NVDA and Intel (INTC) report specific expense amounts for their defined contribution and matching contribution plans. NVDA reports a contribution expense of $255 million for fiscal year 2024. Intel reports matching contribution expenses of $541 million for 2024, noting that the matching rate in the US qualified plan was increased in 2024 compared to prior years. Both disclosures quantify the cost of these retirement benefits to the company, allowing for a direct comparison of the scale of contributions, with Intel's reported matching expense being significantly higher than NVDA's total contribution expense.

sentences.text: Our contribution expense for fiscal years 2024, 2023, and 2022 was $255 million, $227 million, and $168 million, respectively.

We expensed $541 million in 2024, $272 million in 2023, and $489 million in 2022 for matching contributions based on the amount of employee contributions under the US qualified defined contribution and non-qualified deferred compensation plans.
The matching contribution in the US qualified defined contribution plan was increased from January 1 through December 31, 2024 as compared to 2023 and 2022.
